chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Tyree returns for the Masterpieces by Ellington album
summary: Tyree Glenn only came back to record Masterpieces by Ellington with Mood Indigo and Sophisticated Lady, then returned to gigging and the Ted Steele show.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: We got back to the United States and then Tyree come
back and made an album with us, the Masterpieces by Ellington, which is a beautiful album.
Tyree just stayed in New York.

He just stayed in New York and got to gigging around New York and everything and that was right before that he got the Ted Steele show, you see. And he was really doing -- he was doing all right for himself. He wasn't hurting at all.
So then he came back. What year was that he came back?
We came back in '50 and Tyree came back just to make the album and that's all. He wouldn't stay in the band.
What album was that, Butter? Do you remember?
A beautiful album. Three extended versions of Mood Indigo, of Sophisticated Lady, and -- Mood
Oh, that's quite adequate for me, but if you want to name the rest of them.
-- we had the extended version and Billy Strayhorn played piano solos on there.
